title: UPSC CSE - Indian Economy - GDP, GNP
subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
Which of the following activities constitute a real sector in the economy?
1. Farmers harvesting their crops
2. Textile mills converting raw cotton into fabrics
3. A commercial bank lending money to a trading company
4. A corporate body issuing Rupee Denominated Bonds overseas
questions.explain: The real sector of the economy deals with the production side, while the nominal economy deals with the financial side. Financial activities majorly support real(production) activity, (Hence Statement 1 and 2 are correct) but does not contribute itself too much except the factor income it generates (Hence statements 3 and 4 are not correct).
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q: Which among the following steps is most likely to be taken at the time of an economic recession?
options: Cut in tax rates accompanied by increase in interest rate
Increase in expenditure on public projects
Increase in tax rates accompanied by reduction of interest rate
Reduction of expenditure on public projects
questions.explain: A recession is a slowdown or a massive contraction in economic activities. A significant fall in spending generally leads to a recession. Such a slowdown in economic activities may last for some quarters, thereby completely hampering the growth of an economy. In such a situation, economic indicators such as GDP, corporate profits, employment, etc., fall. To tackle the menace, economies generally react by loosening their monetary policies by infusing more money into the system, i.e., by increasing the money supply. During a recession, the government can: Lower interest rates to increase borrowing capacity, increase government spending, and cut tax rates to enhance people's spending capacity.

questions.q: Despite being a high saving economy, capital formation may not result in significant increase in output due to
questions.explain: Capital-output ratio is the amount of capital needed to produce one unit of output. A higher ratio means that more capital is needed to produce one unit of output due to which the increased capital formation may not result in significant increase in output. A higher ratio generally indicates inefficient deployment of the capital resources of a nation.

questions.q: Increase in absolute and per capita real GNP do not connote a higher level of economic development, if
options: industrial output fails to keep pace with agricultural output.
agricultural output fails to keep pace with industrial output.
questions.explain: Per capita real GNP accurately captures the economic growth of a nation by adjusting for price level changes so that the actual growth in the production of goods and services can be understood. By dividing real GNP on a per capita basis, a clearer comparison can be made with other nations having different populations. But, what these measures cannot accurately capture is development. Development happens when the fruits of economic growth are translated into increased prosperity and better standards of living for all the residents of a nation. Increasing poverty and unemployment reflect that the fruits of growth in Real GNP have not adequately spread to all. While economic growth is happening for the nation in general a section of people is left behind hence a higher level of economic development is not taking place in the country.

questions.q: A decrease in the tax to GDP ratio of a country indicates which of the following?\n1. Slowing economic growth rates\n2. Less equitable distribution of national income
questions.explain: A decrease in the tax to GDP ratio of a country indicates the slowing economic growth rates. As economic activities slow down, the economic growth rates also slows down, and this results in fall in income, employment and sales, which directly impacts the direct and indirect tax collection, leading to a lower tax to GDP ratio. Tax to GDP ratio does not uncover the distribution of the income across the country. It presents a sum total picture of all the tax collected from domestic residents to the GDP added by all the domestic residents.

questions.q:
With reference to India economy, consider the following statements:
1. The rate of growth of real Gross Domestic Product has steadily increased in the last decade.
2. The Gross Domestic Product at market prices (in rupees) has steadily increased in the last decade.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Real GDP is the GDP of a country at constant prices. That is, the growth rate of the GDP has been adjusted to remove the impact of change in price levels in comparison to the base year. In India, the rate of growth in real GDP has not steadily increased. The Gross Domestic Product at Market Prices has steadily increased in the past decade. However, the Financial Year 2020-2021 may be an exception due to the fall of GDP caused because of the COVID-19 pandemic.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q: Economic growth in country X will necessarily have to occur if
options: there is technical progress in the world economy
there is population growth in X
there is capital formation in X
the volume of trade grows in the world economy
questions.explain: Economic Growth is the increase in the production of goods and services in an economy over a specified period of time. Attaining economic growth is a primary purpose behind all economic planning. This can be attained by various means. Capital formation, that is the acquisition of new or existing fixed assets that are intended for use in the production of other goods and services for a period of over one year will lead to an increase in the production of goods and services in the economy hence necessarily leading to economic growth.

questions.q: The National Income of a country for a given period is equal to the:
options: Total value of goods and services produced by the nationals.
Sum of total consumption and investment expenditure.
Sum of personal income of all individuals.
Money value of final goods and services produced.
questions.explain: National Income means the sum total of Income that everyone earns in a nation. As the earning of everyone is dependent or directly related to the production of some sorts of goods or services in the economy, hence the money value of final goods and services produced in an economy is the most relevant measure of the National Income of a country.

questions.q:
In the context of Indian economy, consider the following statements:
1. The growth rate of GDP has steadily increased in the last five years.
2. The growth rate in per capita income has steadily increased in the last five years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Although the GDP has grown steadily in the last five years, the growth rate has not steadily increased. It has gone up and down with no definite unidirectional trend. The growth rate in per capita incomes has experienced fluctuation with no unidirectional trend. In fact, the per capita incomes actually fell on a year-on-year basis from 2007 to 2008.
